summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of COPD, alcohol abuse, dementia, recurrent aspiration, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for shortness of breath, fever, and hypotension. He was found to have septic shock due to aspiration pneumonia, requiring ICU admission, vasopressor support, and broad-spectrum antibiotics. He improved rapidly, was weaned off oxygen, and transitioned to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate. His hyponatremia resolved with fluid therapy, and he was restarted on home medications. A Foley catheter was managed with daily voiding trials, and he was discharged to extended care with plans for outpatient speech and swallow therapy, urology follow-up, and repeat endoscopy for a known esophageal ulcer.
problems: Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food and vomit
